- When sentiment is negative and forecast is below recent low, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward slightly to reflect sentiment-driven support.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model overreacts to recent highs — apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overbought mispricing.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model overcorrects downward — increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature bearish reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates upward momentum — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment is positive and recent price is rising.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
